what: Two nested questions. kind: does the mechanism put content into the context window (insertion) or does the context stop working with nothing added (degradation)? agency, defined only for insertion: did an adversary write the content (attack), did a retriever, tool or the agent's own memory deliver it with nobody behind it (accident), or does the paper describe one mechanism reachable both ways (both)?
method: Safety-regime entries hand-coded one by one against the registry name and notes. Security-regime entries screened by keyword for degradation language; all 14 hits read by hand and all insert content, so the regime is recorded as insertion throughout without a full read of 176 entries.

entries.agency_ruling: Hostile content exists upstream, so the default from the safety regime looks wrong. It is not: the named mechanism is the compression step that strips the content of its detectable markers, and the paper frames that step as a non-adversarial incident of how multi-agent systems summarise. The adversary is in the input, not in the mechanism.

method_agency: Default from regime: security insertion reads as attack, safety insertion as accident. All 20 safety-regime insertion entries were read by hand, and so were the 7 security-regime insertion entries whose notes use incidental language (benign, inadvertent, naturally occurring). Three entries are ruled against their default and carry an agency_ruling field.
